comparisons.peer_summary: On July 1, 2024, Broadcom sold its end-user computing (EUC) business to KKR & Co. Inc. for $3.5 billion in cash, as the business was not aligned with strategic objectives. The company has no material continuing involvement with this business and reported its results in discontinued operations.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom disclose strategic restructuring actions regarding specific business units, but they differ in direction and execution stage. AMD is in the pre-closing phase, intending to seek a partner for the manufacturing component of the acquired ZT Systems business, whereas Broadcom has completed the sale of its end-user computing (EUC) business. Broadcom explicitly states the divestiture was because the business was 'not aligned with our strategic objectives,' while AMD's approach involves seeking a 'strategic partner' to acquire the manufacturing arm post-acquisition. Both actions reflect a refocusing of strategic assets, but one is a completed divestiture and the other is an intended post-merger carve-out.

sentences.text: The Company intends to seek a strategic partner to acquire ZT Systems' manufacturing business.
Assets and liabilities held-for-sale primarily included the end-user computing ("EUC") business and certain other assets and liabilities, which were not aligned with our strategic objectives.
On July 1, 2024, we sold the EUC business to KKR & Co. Inc. for cash consideration of $3.5 billion, after working capital adjustments.

comparisons.peer_topic: Implementation of Internal Foundry Operating Model
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel implemented an internal foundry operating model in Q1 2024, creating a foundry relationship between Intel Products (CCG, DCAI, NEX) and Intel Foundry, which involves CPU design/development and manufacturing/services respectively.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel disclose significant changes to their manufacturing strategies involving the Intel Foundry or similar operational models, but they differ in the nature of the change. Intel implemented an internal foundry operating model in Q1 2024 to create a relationship between its Products business and Foundry services. In contrast, AMD is planning to divest the manufacturing business of ZT Systems by seeking a strategic partner, rather than integrating or restructuring it internally. Both highlight a focus on aligning manufacturing capabilities with broader strategic objectives, but Intel's change is an internal organizational shift while AMD's is an external transaction decision.
